title: BradEngine Voxel Engine

contributors.contribution: Jamie used the voxel engine while teaching his 14-year-old son 3D engine, procedural-generation, and world-building concepts.

description: Built on BradEngine's native JavaScript software 3D renderer, the BradEngine Voxel Engine explored chunk-based procedural worlds, Perlin/noise-driven terrain, Web Worker generation, neighbor-aware mesh construction, chunk recycling, persistent voxel state, and runtime world editing through reusable 3D engine systems.

sections.title: Built on BradEngine 3D
paragraphs: The voxel system was a dedicated subsystem built on top of BradEngine's native JavaScript 3D renderer.
Voxel chunks were converted into BradEngine mesh data and rendered through the same software 3D pipeline.

sections.title: Chunk-Based World
paragraphs: The world was divided into reusable voxel chunks instead of being represented as one monolithic mesh.

sections.title: Procedural Terrain
paragraphs: Terrain height was generated procedurally using Perlin/noise-style functions.

sections.title: Web Worker Generation
paragraphs: Chunk terrain generation could run in Web Workers so procedural generation did not have to block the main rendering loop.

sections.title: Neighbor-Aware Surface Extraction
paragraphs: The mesh builder checked neighboring voxel occupancy before generating faces.
Faces hidden between adjacent solid blocks were omitted so only visible voxel surfaces became render geometry.

sections.title: Generated Mesh Optimization
paragraphs: Generated voxel surfaces were converted into reusable mesh structures rather than submitted as isolated cubes.

sections.title: Chunk Streaming / Recycling
paragraphs: Chunks around the active world area could be reused or replaced as the player moved, allowing the system to maintain a bounded working set rather than permanently retaining every generated area.

sections.title: Persistent Voxel State
paragraphs: Voxel chunk data could be stored in browser localStorage so generated or modified terrain could survive between runs.

sections.title: Runtime Voxel Editing
paragraphs: The chunk system supported voxel lookup and modification within active chunks.
Edited chunks could be marked dirty and rebuilt so world changes were reflected in the generated render mesh.

sections.title: World Systems
paragraphs: The voxel project was organized into multiple cooperating systems rather than one procedural demo.

sections.title: Teaching Context
paragraphs: I used the voxel project while teaching my son how larger 3D systems fit together, including chunked worlds, procedural generation, mesh construction, rendering, and runtime state.

historicalNotes: This is the JavaScript BradEngine voxel subsystem; the legacy filename containing 'java-voxel-engine' is misleading.
The legacy card dates the teaching work to Covid 2020 and identifies JavaScript, Canvas, Perlin Noise, Math, WebRTC, and Batch Scripts.
The voxel system was built on BradEngine's custom software 3D renderer.
Voxel-specific architecture is kept on this card rather than the general BradEngine 3D renderer card.
The project used chunk-based world organization, procedural/noise terrain generation, Web Workers, neighbor-aware visible-face generation, chunk recycling, and localStorage-backed state.
Runtime voxel edits could trigger dirty-chunk rebuilds.
